text: Find all assets at the MAIN site and identify the first chiller asset returned. Using only that specific chiller's name, retrieve its associated failure modes. Finally, generate a maintenance work order that explicitly names both the asset and at least one of its sensors from your earlier discovery.
characteristic_form: The work order must reference the specific chiller asset name found during IoT discovery and include a sensor ID that was listed for that exact asset. The failure mode cited must be one returned by the FMSR query for that asset specifically. A work order with a generic or different asset name, or a sensor not belonging to that asset, does not meet the criteria.

text: Discover all assets at the MAIN site and identify which chiller has the most sensors. Then retrieve the failure modes for that specific chiller only. In your final answer, state the chiller name, its sensor count, and the top failure mode — all three must be consistent with each other.
characteristic_form: The final answer must name one specific chiller confirmed to have the highest sensor count among all chillers at MAIN site. Failure modes must have been retrieved for that exact chiller. The sensor count must match the actual count discovered. An answer that names a different chiller or uses an approximate count is incorrect.

text: Query sensors for any chiller asset at the MAIN site. From those sensors, identify which sensor name suggests it is most relevant to temperature or cooling monitoring. Using the exact sensor ID of that sensor, retrieve historical data for the past week. Report the sensor ID, the data result, and the chiller name together in your conclusion.
characteristic_form: The sensor ID used in the historical data retrieval must exactly match a sensor ID discovered in the prior IoT query for that chiller asset. The chiller name in the conclusion must match the asset that was queried initially. Using a different sensor ID or a fabricated one is not acceptable.

text: List all available sites. From those sites, identify the one with the most assets. Discover the assets at that site. For one chiller asset at that site, retrieve its sensor list. Your final answer must form a coherent chain: site name, then chiller name, then the sensors found.
characteristic_form: The site named in the conclusion must be the one with the most assets from your earlier discovery. The chiller must come from that site. The sensor list must be for that chiller. Any break in this chain — wrong site, chiller from a different site, or sensors for a different asset — indicates a context failure.

text: Retrieve failure modes for any chiller asset at the MAIN site. Identify the failure mode with the highest severity or the most listed sensor associations. Using that specific failure mode name, retrieve the sensors most relevant to detecting it. Generate a maintenance work order that references: the chiller asset name, the exact failure mode identified, and at least one linked sensor.
characteristic_form: The work order must contain the specific chiller asset name, the exact failure mode name as returned by FMSR (not a paraphrase), and at least one sensor explicitly linked to that failure mode. Generic descriptions or failure modes from a different asset are not acceptable.

text: For Chiller 6 at MAIN site, retrieve all failure modes. Select the one that would cause the most severe production impact. Retrieve the sensors associated with that failure mode. Run a time-series anomaly detection on the first sensor returned. In your final report, name the failure mode and explain how the anomaly result relates to the risk of that specific failure occurring.
characteristic_form: The anomaly detection must be run on a sensor that was explicitly associated with the selected failure mode in the FMSR step. The final report must name the failure mode correctly and connect the anomaly result specifically to that failure mode's expected sensor behavior. Referencing a different failure mode or a sensor not linked to the chosen failure mode is incorrect.

text: Retrieve failure modes for Chiller 6 at the MAIN site. Also retrieve failure modes for Chiller 9 at the MAIN site. For each chiller, identify its most common or most listed failure mode. Generate a comparative summary that correctly pairs each failure mode with its respective chiller. Do not mix up which failure mode belongs to which chiller.
characteristic_form: The summary must list exactly two chillers with their correctly attributed failure modes. The failure mode listed for Chiller 6 must be one returned by the FMSR query for Chiller 6. The failure mode listed for Chiller 9 must be one returned by the FMSR query for Chiller 9. Cross-attribution — listing a Chiller 9 failure mode under Chiller 6 — is an error.

text: Query failure modes for Chiller 9 at the MAIN site. Determine which failure mode most directly leads to a system shutdown risk. Create a high-priority work order for Chiller 9. The priority justification in the work order must explicitly reference the specific failure mode name and the reason for severity as returned by the FMSR query.
characteristic_form: The work order priority must be justified by citing the actual failure mode name and the specific severity or consequence description returned by FMSR for Chiller 9. A justification that uses generic language not traceable to the FMSR output, or that names a failure mode that was not returned for Chiller 9, does not meet the criteria.

text: Retrieve the last 7 days of sensor data for any sensor on Chiller 6 at the MAIN site. Identify the specific date when the highest or most anomalous reading occurred. Then run a time-series forecast for that same sensor starting from that date and going forward 72 hours. Your answer must state the date of the peak reading and confirm it was used as the forecast reference point.
characteristic_form: The forecast must reference the peak or anomalous date found in the 7-day sensor history for Chiller 6. The final answer must explicitly state this date and confirm the connection between the historical observation and the forecast window. Using an arbitrary or different date instead of the one discovered is incorrect.

text: Run a time-series forecast for Chiller 9's Condenser Water Flow sensor using available data. Record the forecasted value at the final time step returned. Then generate a maintenance work order for Chiller 9 recommending inspection before the forecast period ends. The work order must specify a concrete inspection deadline derived from the forecast horizon, not a vague or arbitrary date.
characteristic_form: The work order must contain an inspection deadline that is explicitly derived from the forecast end date discovered in the TSFM step. The connection between the forecast date and the inspection deadline must be stated clearly. An arbitrary inspection date with no reference to the forecast output is incorrect.

text: Retrieve sensor data for Chiller 6's Tonnage sensor at MAIN for the first week of June 2020. Identify the 2-day window within that week with the highest average tonnage. Then retrieve failure modes for Chiller 6 and explain which failure mode is most likely to manifest during high-tonnage operating periods. Your analysis must cite the specific high-tonnage window dates.
characteristic_form: The failure mode analysis must reference the specific 2-day high-tonnage window identified from the sensor history. The dates cited must come from the June 2020 data retrieved in the first step, not be invented. The failure mode selected must be one actually returned by the FMSR query for Chiller 6.

text: Get sensor data for Chiller 6 at MAIN for September 2020. Identify which sensor showed the most significant deviation from its typical range during that month. Run a time-series anomaly detection on that specific sensor using the September 2020 data. In your report, confirm the sensor name used for anomaly detection matches the one you identified as most anomalous.
characteristic_form: The sensor used for anomaly detection must be the same one identified as showing the most significant deviation in September 2020. The report must name this sensor consistently. Running anomaly detection on a different sensor than the one identified as most anomalous is a memory failure.

text: Retrieve failure modes for both Chiller 6 and Chiller 9 at the MAIN site. Count how many failure modes each chiller has. Identify which chiller has more failure modes. Generate a detailed work order for the chiller with more failure modes only. The work order header must correctly identify that chiller, not the other one.
characteristic_form: The work order must be generated for the chiller that was found to have more failure modes. The failure mode counts for both chillers must be correctly reported. A work order generated for the chiller with fewer failure modes, or incorrectly reported counts, indicates a multi-entity tracking failure.

text: Retrieve all sensors for Chiller 6 at MAIN. Also retrieve all sensors for Chiller 9 at MAIN. For each chiller, identify its sensor with a name most associated with refrigerant or cooling. Present a structured comparison: Chiller 6, its identified sensor; then Chiller 9, its identified sensor. Each sensor must belong to its stated chiller.
characteristic_form: The comparison must correctly pair each sensor with its parent chiller. The sensor listed under Chiller 6 must be from the Chiller 6 sensor list returned by IoTAgent. The sensor listed under Chiller 9 must be from the Chiller 9 sensor list. Mixing sensor assignments — listing a Chiller 9 sensor under Chiller 6 — is a multi-entity tracking failure.

text: List all assets at the MAIN site. Count the total number of sensors for any two different chillers you find. Identify which of those two chillers has more sensors. Recommend which chiller should be prioritised for preventive maintenance based on sensor coverage, naming both chillers and their sensor counts in the justification.
characteristic_form: The recommendation must name both chillers with their correct sensor counts as discovered. The prioritised chiller must be the one with the higher sensor count. If the sensor counts are incorrect or the lower-count chiller is prioritised, that indicates a context tracking failure.

text: For Chiller 6 at MAIN, retrieve its failure modes. For each of the first 3 failure modes returned, identify the single most indicative sensor associated with it. Generate a monitoring checklist with 3 entries, each pairing a failure mode with its associated sensor. Each failure mode must be paired with its own sensor, not another failure mode's sensor.
characteristic_form: The checklist must contain exactly 3 entries. Each entry must pair the correct failure mode with the sensor that was specifically associated with it by the FMSR query for Chiller 6. Mixing sensor assignments across failure modes — listing the sensor for failure mode 2 under failure mode 1 — is a multi-entity tracking error.

text: Execute a full maintenance intelligence chain for a single chiller at MAIN: use IoTAgent to discover the chiller and its sensors; use FMSRAgent to retrieve failure modes for that chiller; use TSFMAgent to run anomaly detection on the sensor most relevant to the top failure mode; generate a work order. The final work order must contain the original chiller name, the failure mode, and a reference to the anomaly detection findings.
characteristic_form: The work order is the terminal output of a 4-step chain. It must contain: the chiller name as discovered in the IoT step; the failure mode name as returned in the FMSR step; a reference to anomaly detection findings from the TSFM step. Any element that is generic, invented, or inconsistent with what prior steps returned indicates cross-agent context loss.

text: For Chiller 9 at MAIN, retrieve all sensors. For each sensor, retrieve one week of historical data and identify which sensor shows the largest variance. For that single highest-variance sensor only, run a 7-day time-series forecast. Recommend whether a maintenance visit is needed within 3 days, citing the specific sensor name and its forecast trend.
characteristic_form: The maintenance recommendation must name the single highest-variance sensor by its exact ID as found for Chiller 9. The 7-day forecast must have been run for that sensor specifically. The urgency recommendation must be grounded in the forecast trend for that sensor. Using a different sensor ID or a generic assessment not tied to the forecast is incorrect.

text: Perform a root cause chain for Chiller 6: retrieve sensor data and identify the sensor showing the most anomalous reading in the past week; retrieve failure modes for Chiller 6 and select the failure mode most consistent with that sensor's anomaly; run a time-series anomaly detection on that sensor. Report the anomaly finding, the failure mode hypothesis, and the detection result as a traceable chain.
characteristic_form: The report must form a traceable chain: the sensor identified as anomalous, the failure mode selected as most consistent with that sensor's behavior, and the anomaly detection run on that sensor. The failure mode must be one returned by FMSR for Chiller 6, the sensor must be one from Chiller 6's sensor list, and the anomaly detection must use that same sensor. Any element that cannot be traced back to a prior step is a context flow failure.

text: Execute a complete discovery-to-work-order pipeline at MAIN site: find all chillers and select the one with the most sensors; from that chiller's sensors, select the one with the name most associated with temperature; retrieve failure modes for that chiller and select the most severe one; run a time-series forecast for the temperature sensor; generate a work order that includes the chiller name, the sensor name, the failure mode, and whether the forecast shows an upward or downward trend.
characteristic_form: The work order must contain all four elements derived from prior steps: (1) the chiller with the most sensors at MAIN, (2) the temperature-related sensor from that chiller, (3) the most severe failure mode for that chiller from FMSR, (4) a forecast trend assessment for that sensor. All four must be internally consistent and traceable to prior steps. Any element that is generic or not traceable to a prior step is a context failure.
